title: A Bird That Stayed in the Air for 200 Days Straight

scenes.text: One bird never touches the ground for six months.
Alpine swifts were tracked staying airborne for more than 200 days in a row.
No landing. No perching. They catch insects mid-air.
Sensors showed them flapping, then gliding for minutes with barely a wingbeat.
They breed in Europe, then cross to Africa and stay up there all winter.
So where does a bird rest, when it never lands?

description:
One bird never touches the ground for six months.
Tracking tags showed alpine swifts staying in the air for more than 200 straight days, feeding on insects as they fly.
What would you do if you could never land?
first_comment: Could you go one day without sitting down? These birds skip six months.
